# WhatsApp

<!-- Generated by `pnpm whatsapp:doc` from src/lib/whatsapp/events.ts. Do not hand-edit the table. -->

One event sends a WhatsApp message. It is off until an administrator switches it on at **Masters & Users →
WhatsApp**, and needs an approved template — the words are in
[WHATSAPP_TEMPLATES.md](WHATSAPP_TEMPLATES.md).

## The trigger

| # | Event | Fires when | Goes to | Template | Vars |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **A site visit is booked**<br>`SITE_VISIT_SCHEDULED` | A site visit is scheduled against a lead | The client whose visit it is _(customer — outside the organisation)_ | `site_visit_conformatioon` | 6 |

## Where it is raised

| Event | In the code |
|---|---|
| `SITE_VISIT_SCHEDULED` | `lib/sales/site-visit-alert.ts` → `tellClientAboutSiteVisit()`, which composes it and sends it. Two actions call it: `sales/site-visits/actions.ts` → `scheduleSiteVisitAction` (the form), and `sales/leads/actions.ts` → `logFollowUpAction` when a follow-up is logged as a site visit, carrying the date typed on it. **Moving a lead to the Site Visit stage sends nothing** — the board holds no time, so the only message it could raise would read "When: —". The same visit logged twice is sent once: it is matched on the time it names |

## How it travels

1. The business flow calls `enqueueWhatsApp()`, which writes one row in
   `whatsapp_messages` — or nothing, if the trigger is off. **It never throws**:
   a booking must not fail because a template was renamed.
2. **The action sends it there and then**, on an eight-second deadline. The
   client is told while the person who scheduled the visit is still looking at
   the screen, and a provider having a slow minute delays the message rather
   than failing the visit.
3. `POST /api/whatsapp/dispatch` runs every five minutes from cron and sweeps
   up whatever the first attempt did not get: a timeout, a 5xx, a rate limit,
   anything queued while the connection was off. It also runs the overdue-task
   sweep, which rings the in-app bell and sends no WhatsApp — that sweep had
   tests and no caller until this endpoint existed.
4. A refusal about the message itself (400: template not approved, number not on
   WhatsApp) is final. Their outage (5xx, 429) or an unreachable host is tried
   again after 2, then 8, then 32 minutes, four attempts in all.
5. Every message stays as a row, sent or not. The log on the WhatsApp tab is
   that table.

## The connection

**Masters & Users → WhatsApp → Connection.** Nothing lives in an environment
variable, because a token in one needs a deploy to rotate and this one does not
— it is read fresh on every send.

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| API url | `https://graph.facebook.com` for Meta direct, or a BSP's own base url. A BSP that proxies Meta (BotSyncWA, 360dialog, Gupshup) needs nothing else changed. |
| Version | `v21.0` for Meta. A BSP may pin its own. |
| Phone number id | The id of the sending number, not the number. |
| WhatsApp Business Account id | Only to read approved templates back from Meta. A BSP that keeps templates in its own portal has none. |
| Access token | Write-only. The screen is told whether one is set and its last four characters, never the token. |
| Send WhatsApp messages | Off, nothing is sent and nothing is queued. The triggers keep their settings. |

A trigger cannot be switched on unless its template is **approved** at Meta —
otherwise it would queue messages that can never leave.

## Installing the cron

```bash
# on the server, once
echo 'WHATSAPP_CRON_SECRET=<a long random string>' >> /var/www/nninfra/app/.env
install -m 644 deploy/nninfra-whatsapp.cron /etc/cron.d/nninfra-whatsapp
pm2 restart nninfra           # so the app reads the new variable
```

Without `WHATSAPP_CRON_SECRET` the endpoint refuses every call, which is what
an unconfigured host should do. The sweeps then never run — including the
overdue-task notices, which this endpoint is also the only caller of.

## When it does not send

- **The same visit twice.** The time is what makes it the same message: a
  client scheduled on the form and then dragged to Site Visit on the board
  hears once. A *changed* time is news and is sent.
- **A lead moved to Site Visit with no time on it.** The board captures none,
  so one is looked for — the soonest visit already booked against the lead, or
  its next action if that is still ahead. With neither, nothing is sent: a
  confirmation that cannot name a time is not a confirmation. The log carries
  a skipped row saying so, rather than leaving somebody waiting for a message
  that was never coming.

## What is deliberately not here

- **The other eight triggers.** Approvals pending, overdue tasks, denied
  checklist points, lapsed follow-ups, bounced receipts, expiring holds, a
  vendor's purchase order and a customer's receipt and booking were all built
  and are in the history — this release sends the one alert that was asked for.
  Each is a registry entry and one call to put back.
- **Delivery receipts.** Meta's webhook can say *delivered* and *read*;
  `metaMessageId` is stored against every sent row so it can be matched later,
  but nothing consumes the webhook yet.
- **Opt-in records.** The three outside events — a vendor's order, a customer's
  receipt and their booking — need the recipient to have agreed beforehand.
  Where that is recorded is not decided.
- **Quiet hours**, and a per-person choice of which events reach them.
